interim_publication_reason: Reuters published an investigation within the coverage window reporting a breach of the U.S. Air Force's Cloud One multi-cloud platform and describing operational disruption.

source_audit.verification_note: The Reuters article was opened and checked for its 2026-11-27 11:01 UTC publication time, source attribution, operational claims and limitations. The CBS follow-up was opened and checked for its 2026-11-27 9:44 PM EST update time and the Air Force/DoD statements it quotes. CBS relies on Reuters for the breach account and is not an independent technical confirmation. The Air Force did not confirm or deny the specific incident. No named vulnerability, provider-specific compromise, attacker identity, data-exfiltration finding or financial impact was established. No 100% verification claim is made.

research_findings.topic: U.S. Air Force Cloud One reported security incident
research_findings.caveat: Reuters attributes the breach to three people familiar with the matter. CBS obtained additional official comments but relies on Reuters for the breach account. The affected provider layer, vulnerability, attacker, scope and any data theft remain unknown.

Reuters describes Cloud One as combining Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Alphabet services. No source identifies which provider or layer was affected. Do not infer compromise of Azure, AWS, Google Cloud or Oracle Cloud.

priority_company_scan.note: Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet are relevant through Reuters' description of Cloud One's provider mix, but no company-specific operating disclosure or provider-specific compromise was established.
